heroLead: Whites City sits right at the entrance to Carlsbad Caverns National Park, and while most visitors passing through are headed underground for the scenery, the ground beneath the surrounding ranchland has its own story in the Delaware Basin.
intro: Eddy County has been one of the more actively drilled counties on the New Mexico side of the Permian, with Wolfcamp and Bone Spring horizontal development extending across much of the county outside the park boundary itself. If your family's minerals are near Whites City, they may well be part of that broader activity even though the immediate area is best known for the caverns.

sections.heading: Park boundary versus surrounding minerals
paragraphs: Carlsbad Caverns National Park itself is federally protected and off-limits to drilling, but private and state minerals just outside the park boundary in Eddy County have seen substantial horizontal development in recent years. If your interest sits outside the park itself, it's worth checking current activity rather than assuming the protected status of the caverns extends to your acreage.

sections.heading: Ranching-family ownership near the park
paragraphs: A lot of the land around Whites City has stayed in ranching families for generations, and mineral ownership here often follows the same pattern seen across Eddy County — split among heirs, sometimes with incomplete paperwork, but still traceable through county records.

sections.heading: New Mexico's oil conservation rules apply here too
paragraphs: Even this close to a national park, drilling on private and state minerals outside the boundary follows the same New Mexico Oil Conservation Division permitting and spacing rules as the rest of Eddy County. That means a tract near Whites City isn't automatically treated any differently just because of its scenic neighbor.
If you own a fractional interest here and aren't sure whether it falls inside or outside the protected boundary, that's the first thing we confirm before discussing value.

faqs.question: Does being near Carlsbad Caverns National Park mean my minerals can't be drilled?
faqs.answer: Only if your specific tract falls within the federally protected park boundary. Minerals outside that boundary in Eddy County have seen substantial development. We check your tract's specific location before answering.

faqs.question: Is Eddy County an active drilling area?
faqs.answer: Yes, it's been one of the more heavily drilled counties in the New Mexico Delaware Basin. We check current permits near your specific tract to confirm.

faqs.question: My family's ownership near Whites City is unclear. Can you help sort it out?
faqs.answer: Yes, we work with a title company using Eddy County records to confirm ownership, even starting from incomplete paperwork.
